processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under argon.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10×5×2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere followed by oil quenching; this is the parent process of the aging treatment.
Solution-treated sample aged at 550 °C for 6 h followed by water quenching; this is the terminal state defining this sample (hardness 778.5 ± 23.7 HV).

structures.overall_structure: Solution-treated 19Al alloy is a single α (BCC) phase; raising Al from 15 to 19 at.% markedly refines the grain structure.

Partially transformed structure for 19Al after aging at 550 °C for 6 h: the α (BCC) matrix is only partly converted; β-Mn precipitates as a network along α grain boundaries plus short rod-shaped precipitates inside α grains, and untransformed α remains; α-Mn is also present. XRD of this exact condition shows α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn.

phases_present.morphology: untransformed matrix (labelled 'Untransformed α' in the 550 °C-6 h SE image)
network along α grain boundaries and short rod-shaped precipitates within α grains
fine particles dispersed in the α matrix

precipitates.distribution: along α grain boundaries and within α grains (short rod-shaped)
fine particles dispersed in the α matrix

interfaces.phase_evolution: During aging the α matrix progressively transforms to β-Mn; for the 19Al alloy at 550 °C full α→β-Mn transformation requires 10 h, so after 6 h at 550 °C untransformed α coexists with β-Mn and α-Mn. The overall microstructural evolution sequence proposed for the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu system is α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase.
interfaces.interface_notes: At the β-Mn interfaces of the ultra-hard alloys (peak-hardness states), new BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase form; the FCC Cu-rich phase content between β-Mn interfaces decreased with increasing Al content. These interphase precipitates were characterised on peak-hardness samples rather than specifically on the 19Al 550 °C/6 h state.

measurement_conditions.test_standard: Vickers microhardness, load 9.8 N for 15 s; average of 5 measurements

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: aging hardening response / hardness after aging

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 repeated tests averaged per sample
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure hardness after solution treatment and different aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al aged at 550 °C for 6 h: 778.5 ± 23.7 HV; solution-treated baseline 263.8 ± 1.1 HV
The 19Al 550 °C × 6 h trace (blue) contains α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn, showing α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before the α matrix fully transformed

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE imaging, 50 µm main-panel scale bars (550 °C-6 h panel); 100 µm for 550 °C-3 h
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: 550 °C-6 h panel shows a partially transformed structure with untransformed α labelled

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.purpose: Map constituent phases and orientations after different aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy, at aging temperatures progressing with time the α matrix progressively transforms to β-Mn; e.g. 525 °C/10 h gives a thin β-Mn network in α, while 600 °C/3 h and 650 °C/6 h give almost pure β-Mn with new FCC/BCC precipitates

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the microstructures/pHases of the ultra-high-hardness alloys (performed on 15Al 600 °C/6 h and 17Al 575 °C/6 h, not on the 19Al 550 °C/6 h sample)
characterization_methods.key_findings: FCC Cu-rich particles with FCC twins form at the β-Mn interfaces; β-Mn is poor in Cu

unmapped_findings: At 550 °C the α→β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy is not complete after 6 h; the 19Al alloy requires 10 h at 550 °C to fully transform (by contrast the 17Al alloy fully transforms after 6 h at 550 °C) — this timing constrains the interpretation of the 19Al 550 °C/6 h state.

The nanoindentation hardness values (19Al hardest sample H_Ave = 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa), the intrinsic β-Mn hardness (19Al = 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa), the SEM-EDS β-Mn composition of the hardest 19Al sample (Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 17.5 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%) and the fracture toughness KIC (19Al = 3.5 MPa·m1/2) reported in the paper were all measured on the hardest state of the 19Al alloy (600 °C/10 h, 917.8 HV), not on the 19Al 550 °C/6 h sample, so they are not attributed to this sample.

The interphase new BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates at β-Mn interfaces are documented for the ultra-hard (fully transformed) states, e.g. 19Al at 600 °C/3 h and 650 °C/6 h (Fig. 6), rather than for the partially transformed 19Al 550 °C/6 h sample.
